narrative.summary: Turkmenistan has no AI law, AI strategy or AI guidance in force. The only relevant law is the 2017 Law on Information about Private Life and its Protection, which has no rules on automated decisions. A national AI strategy is being drafted by the Ministry of Communications under the 2026-2028 Digital Economy State Programme, whose text has not been published.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The digital economy programme and the draft AI strategy have no published official text and are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Şahsy durmuş barada maglumat we ony goramak hakynda
instruments.english_title: Law of Turkmenistan on Information about Private Life and its Protection
instruments.issuing_authority: Mejlis of Turkmenistan (adopted); signed by the President of Turkmenistan
instruments.current_status: Law No. 519-V of 20 March 2017, published in the Gazette of the Mejlis of Turkmenistan (2017, No. 1, art. 25); in force since 1 July 2017 (art. 33). The Ministry of Justice legal database carries the text without amendment notes as of 12 October 2026. It is Turkmenistan's general personal-data law; it contains no AI-specific or automated-decision provisions. An official Russian version is published alongside the Turkmen text.
instruments.summary: Turkmenistan's personal-data law governs the collection, processing and protection of 'information about private life' (personal data, including biometric data) by state bodies and other operators of personal databases. It requires the data subject's consent except in listed cases, sets rules for depersonalisation, storage, distribution via the internet and cross-border transfer (allowed only to states that protect personal data, or with written consent and other listed exceptions), and gives subjects rights of access and correction. The Cabinet of Ministers sets policy and may create an authorised body to protect data subjects' rights, while the Prosecutor General supervises compliance; there is no rule on automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data-protection law that governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems in Turkmenistan; no AI-specific provisions.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Turkmenistan's Ministry of Justice legal database, the list of laws passed by the Mejlis (parliament), government news sites, ministries and the central bank were searched. Apart from the 2017 personal data law, no qualifying AI-governance document was found; a digital economy programme and a national AI strategy being drafted are listed as leads because no official full text is published. The national cybersecurity site remains to be checked, and the education and health ministries were checked only through general web searches.

leads.english_title: State Programme for the Development of the Digital Economy in Turkmenistan for 2026–2028 and its action plan (with the 2026–2028 Digital Economy Concept)
leads.issuing_authority: President of Turkmenistan (resolution); Ministry of Communications
leads.note: Approved by presidential resolution after the 30 January 2026 government meeting (reported 2 February 2026 on the official sites oilgas.gov.tm and metbugat.gov.tm, news only). The presenting Deputy Chairman said its tasks include developing a national AI strategy, applying AI in industries and training AI specialists. No official full text of the programme, concept or resolution found on minjust.gov.tm, mincom.gov.tm, fineconomic.gov.tm or turkmenistan.gov.tm on 2026-10-12; record as strategy (AI pillar) once the text is published.

leads.english_title: Resolution of the President of Turkmenistan No. 984 of 30 November 2018 approving the Concept for the Development of the Digital Economy in Turkmenistan for 2019–2025
leads.note: Title, number and date confirmed in an official citation (Ministry of Justice order No. 3 of 7 February 2022, minjust.gov.tm document 705). Period ended in 2025; succeeded by the 2026–2028 Concept/State Programme. Secondary sources say it covers AI among digital technologies, but no official full text was found online (minjust.gov.tm legal database and Digital economy page, mincom.gov.tm); would be 'historical' + 'strategy' if the text is published. The companion State Programme for the Development of the Digital Economy 2021–2025 is likewise not published online.
